steps.say: To round to the nearest whole number, look at the tenths digit. 0 to 4 rounds down, and 5 to 9 rounds up.

figure.alt: A number line from 7 to 8 in tenths with 7.6 marked.

steps.say: 7.6 has 6 tenths, so it is closer to 8 than to 7.
To round to one decimal place, look at the hundredths digit.
4.73 is between 4.7 and 4.8. The hundredths digit is 3, so it rounds down to 4.7.

figure.alt: A number line from 4.7 to 4.8 in hundredths with 4.73 marked.

steps.say: Take care with 9s. 3.96 rounded to one decimal place is 4.0.

check.prompt: Round 12.7 to the nearest whole number.
hints: Find the two whole numbers that 12.7 sits between.
check.explanation: 12.7 has 7 tenths, so it rounds up to 13.

hints: One decimal place means one digit after the point.
check.explanation: 5.34 is between 5.3 and 5.4. The hundredths digit is 4, so it rounds down to 5.3.

options.why: The hundredths digit is 4, so the tenths digit stays the same.
That is the nearest whole number, not one decimal place.
One decimal place means only a tenths digit.

check.prompt: A bag of rice has a mass of 2.65 kg. Round its mass to one decimal place.
hints: A digit of 5 or more rounds up.
2.65 is exactly halfway between two tenths.
check.explanation: The hundredths digit is 5, so 2.65 rounds up to 2.7 kg.
